title.en: Dielectric surface: wood, stone and painted parts

summary: Author nonmetal surfaces through finish, grain direction and controlled highlight comparisons.
objective: Orbit the camera: the object remains readable and its finish differs visibly from the adjacent metal part.
example_prompts: Author nonmetal surfaces through finish, grain direction and controlled highlight comparisons.

principles: Choose a surface story: cut timber, worn stone or painted shell. Do not use random noise as a substitute for fabrication direction.
Mechanical friction and optical roughness are separate scene decisions.
implementation: For a nonmetal baseline use metalness 0; compare roughness candidates on the same object under a fixed light rig.
Align authored wood grain with the member length and keep mortar scale consistent across adjacent walls.
Reserve geometric relief for silhouette-changing chips; normal maps alter lighting rather than mesh shape.
observable_checks: Orbit the camera: the object remains readable and its finish differs visibly from the adjacent metal part.
Inspect a silhouette close-up; detail claimed as geometry actually appears at the edge.

known_limits: PBR settings do not identify species, strength, friction or measured surface properties.
Authored reusable guidance; no runtime artifact or improvement has been observed for this record.
creative_affordances: Adapt proportions, finish and presentation to the scene; explain deliberate departures from this guidance.

claims.statement: MeshStandardMaterial uses metalness 0 for nonmetals; normal maps change shading without changing geometry.
